summary: The paper proposes a VQ-VAE + mutual-information pipeline to study planning-related structure in LM hidden states, applied to CFG, path-finding, and OpenWebText, and to compare NTP vs MTP training. The framework is a reasonable methodological contribution and the paper is careful about interpreting nMI comparatively rather than absolutely. However, empirical scope is thin (essentially one small architecture, ~125M with one 0.3B sanity check), a key finding is null (no consistent NTP/MTP difference), several results are confirmatory of prior work (recency, late-layer concentration), and the central methodological claim—that VQ-VAE-based MI avoids probing confounds—is defended only in appendix and does not clearly rule out that the trained VQ-VAE itself acts as a probe with its own capacity-dependent biases.
strengths: Well-motivated question: planning horizon and branch awareness are interesting axes and the paper articulates them cleanly, connecting to MPC/world-model literature.

The VQ-VAE + count-based MI pipeline is a sensible engineering choice for reducing dimensionality and enabling comparable MI estimates across settings; the added cosine/entropy losses to prevent codebook collapse are reasonable.

Careful scoping of claims: authors explicitly restrict interpretation to relative nMI within a setting rather than absolute planning scores, and acknowledge that coarse-graining destroys absolute meaning.

The branch-awareness experiment on PF with disjoint alt/decoy paths is a clean design that meaningfully addresses the 'does the model retain unused correct continuations' question, and the alt/decoy ratio with mean±std is a useful summary.

Multiple task types (symbolic grammar, structured search, natural text) with distinct planning demands, providing at least some evidence that horizon findings are task-contingent rather than an artifact of one benchmark.

Diagnostic in §3.3 combining unconditional and conditional nMI across layers/blocks is a nice touch: the conditional analysis usefully attributes much of block-1 dependence to the final prefix position.

key_concerns.issue: Scale and architectural breadth are very limited. Nearly all conclusions come from GPT-3-Small-sized models trained from scratch, with a single 0.3B check for one plot. Planning behavior—especially the MTP vs NTP comparison and the branch-awareness ratio—may look very different at ≥1B or with modern architectures/instruction tuning, yet the paper frames its findings as 'LMs' broadly.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add at least one substantially larger scale (e.g., 1B–3B) and, if feasible, one pretrained public model (matched by architecture), and either show the trends hold or scope the abstract/intro to 'small transformer LMs trained from scratch on these tasks'.

key_concerns.issue: The core methodological claim that VQ-VAE-based MI 'avoids probe-induced confounds' is under-supported. A trained VQ-VAE is itself a learned mapping whose codebook size, encoder capacity, and training objective determine what information survives quantization; the estimated I(Z_A;Z_B) is therefore bounded by log|codebook| and shaped by encoder capacity in a way conceptually analogous to probe capacity. The rebuttal to probing is deferred to App. D.2–D.5 and to a validation study in App. A.4.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Move a distilled version of the probing-vs-VQ-VAE comparison and the codebook-size / encoder-capacity sensitivity study into the main text; show that qualitative rankings (e.g., decay shape in Fig. 3, alt/decoy ratio ordering in Table 1) are invariant to K and to encoder depth. Otherwise, the framework may inherit exactly the confounds it claims to avoid.

key_concerns.issue: The NTP vs MTP comparison—prominently motivated in the intro—produces a largely null result ('no consistent differences'), yet the paper does not report the effect sizes or seed-level variance needed to make 'no difference' a defensible claim. Table 1 has mean±std but the horizon curves in Fig. 3 are described qualitatively; there is no significance test, no confidence bands, no discussion of statistical power.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report per-seed nMI curves with shaded CIs, run at least 3–5 seeds per condition, and provide either a paired test or Bayes-factor-style analysis before claiming 'no consistent difference'. Alternatively, reframe the NTP/MTP question as exploratory.

key_concerns.issue: Findings in §3.3 (late layers and recent tokens carry most decision-relevant information) largely reproduce well-established observations (recency, late-layer specialization; the paper itself cites Pal et al. 2023, Sukhbaatar et al. 2019, Beltagy et al. 2020). Without a novel prescription or a surprising quantitative finding, this section reads as a demonstration of the pipeline rather than a contribution.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Either (a) use the diagnostic to make a novel, actionable claim (e.g., predict which architectural changes improve which capability) and validate it, or (b) shorten §3.3 and re-scope it explicitly as a worked example of the pipeline rather than as a research finding.

key_concerns.issue: The path-finding tasks are small (28-node vocab, path lengths 4/6) and the 'backward from goal' interpretation of the horizon peak at the second intermediate node is speculative. Without a manipulation (e.g., swapping start/goal, varying graph density) the causal story is a plausible reading of one nMI shape.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add a controlled manipulation—reverse the direction, vary path length continuously, or vary graph branching factor—to test whether the nMI peak tracks 'proximity to the fixed endpoint' as the reverse-planning hypothesis predicts.

key_concerns.issue: Reproducibility of the pipeline hinges on many VQ-VAE hyperparameters (K, λ_q, λ_cos, λ_ent, encoder/decoder depth, block size 16) whose sensitivity is asserted but not shown in the main text. The validation experiment in App. A.4 is referenced but not summarized.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add a compact main-text table with the sensitivity of the headline quantities (Fig. 3 decay slope, Table 1 alt/decoy ratio) to K∈{64,256,1024} and to block size, so readers can see the qualitative claims are robust without hunting through the appendix.

key_concerns.issue: Presentation issues: several places have missing spaces / concatenation artifacts (e.g., 'long-range gen-eration', 'GS toa') and section cross-references appear as bare numbers (' 3.1'). While partially an extraction artifact, some appear intrinsic (e.g., inconsistent LaTeX macros for §, footnote spacing).
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Do a careful pass on cross-references and spacing; ensure section symbols render and that no equations or captions have collapsed tokens.

questions_for_authors: How sensitive are the qualitative conclusions (Fig. 3 decay shape; Table 1 alt/decoy > 1) to codebook size K and to VQ-VAE encoder capacity? Do the orderings survive when K is varied by an order of magnitude?

In App. D.2, does a well-tuned probe (e.g., an MLP with matched parameter count to the VQ-VAE encoder) produce systematically different qualitative conclusions from your MI estimator, or only different absolute numbers?
For the NTP-vs-MTP comparison, what is the seed-level variance of the reported nMI curves, and how many seeds were run? Would a paired test across seeds support the 'no consistent difference' claim?

The prefix-summary code Z^{1:L-1}_{1:T} aggregates all prefix hidden states across layers and positions into a single discrete code. Doesn't this discard the very structure needed to distinguish 'the model plans ahead' from 'the prefix trivially constrains future tokens by grammar/graph edges'? How do you rule out the latter for CFG and PF?

The 'backwards-from-goal' interpretation of the PF-Short horizon peak is intriguing but observational. Have you tested it with a controlled manipulation (swap start/goal; make start unfixed and goal fixed, and vice versa)?
How do the horizon results depend on model scale? The single 0.3B check is on CFG only—does the 0.3B model still show fast nMI decay, or does the horizon extend?
For OpenWebText, why is the horizon analysis (§3.1) not run? Presenting horizon results only on synthetic tasks weakens the case that the framework tells us anything about natural-language planning.
calibration_check: Claims are generally scoped correctly to relative nMI within a setting, but the abstract/intro framing ('planning in LMs', 'general-purpose pipeline') overreaches given that all evidence comes from small from-scratch models on three tasks with a null NTP/MTP result.

significance.justification: Interesting framing of planning as horizon + branch awareness, but the empirical payoff is modest: a null NTP/MTP result and mostly confirmatory findings about recency/late-layer concentration.

novelty.justification: The VQ-VAE + count-based MI + conditional MI application to LM planning analysis is a novel combination, though each component is individually well-known and MI-based interpretability has precedents (Voita, Skean, etc.).

rigor.justification: Method is internally coherent and the relative-only interpretation is disciplined, but the claim of avoiding probing confounds is under-defended in the main text and the pipeline has many degrees of freedom (codebook, encoder capacity, block size) that could shape results.

statistical_soundness.justification: Multiple seeds are mentioned and Table 1 reports mean±std, but the horizon curves in Fig. 3 lack shaded CIs, there are no significance tests, and 'no consistent NTP/MTP difference' is stated without effect-size or power analysis.

calibration_honesty.justification: The paper is unusually careful about limitations of absolute MI values, restricts claims to within-setting comparisons, and acknowledges that findings are aggregate rather than per-prompt.

clarity.justification: The method is explained but with extraction/formatting artifacts, several critical comparisons (probing, VQ-VAE sensitivity, validation) live entirely in the appendix, and the discussion of the aggregate prefix code Z^{1:L-1}_{1:T} does not clearly distinguish 'planning' from 'prefix constrains future by construction'.

structure_compliance.justification: Standard conference structure (intro, method, three-part analysis, conclusion) with appropriate related-work coverage; within reasonable ICLR length.

reproducibility.justification: Model sizes, training objectives, dataset construction, VQ-VAE loss composition, and code/hyperparameter conventions are described sufficiently in principle; missing sensitivity tables in the main text and heavy reliance on appendix material are the main gaps.

related_work.justification: Reasonable coverage of mechanistic interpretability, probing, and information-theoretic analyses; positioning against Pal et al. and probing critiques is clear, though newer MI-based interpretability work could be more directly contrasted quantitatively rather than just cited.

figure_quality.justification: From captions, figures directly support the horizon (Fig. 3), branch-awareness (Table 1), and layer/block heatmap (Fig. 4) claims; missing error bands on horizon curves and the aggregated 'Z^{1:L-1}_{1:T}' visualization limit interpretability.

breadth_generality.justification: Essentially one architecture at one scale (GPT-3 Small, from scratch) with a single 0.3B sanity check on one task; three datasets are used but the generality claims about 'LM planning' outrun the evidence, especially since the horizon analysis on OWT is not fully surfaced.

overall_recommendation.justification: Borderline reject: methodologically thoughtful and honest about scope, but too limited in scale, too reliant on appendix defenses of its core methodological claim, and produces a mix of null and confirmatory results that don't yet clear the ICLR acceptance bar.
